title: ～ぶりに — for the first time in ～ (a period)
summary: Shows that something happened again after a certain length of time: “for the first time in ten years.” It attaches to a word for a period of time (十年, 三年, 一週間). It expresses a feeling of “after so long.”

patterns.form: 期間を表す名詞 ＋ ぶりに ＋ 動詞
patterns.gloss: period + ぶりに: 十年ぶりに帰った
久しぶりに = after a long time (fixed expression)

body.p: The period is the gap since the last time. 十年ぶりに故郷へ帰りました means ten years had passed since the last visit. The feeling is often emotional or positive, like a reunion or a return of good weather.

The period must be a measurable length (a specific time), and the action has happened before. It is not used for something happening for the first time ever. Do not use it for a very short span, like 五分ぶりに.

examples.ja: 十年（じゅうねん）ぶりに故郷（こきょう）へ帰（かえ）りました。
examples.romaji: Jūnen buri ni kokyō e kaerimashita.
examples.tr: I returned to my hometown for the first time in ten years.

examples.ja: 三年（さんねん）ぶりに友（とも）だちと再会（さいかい）した。
examples.romaji: Sannen buri ni tomodachi to saikai shita.
examples.tr: I met my friend again for the first time in three years.

examples.ja: 一週間（いっしゅうかん）ぶりに晴（は）れて、洗濯物（せんたくもの）を干（ほ）した。
examples.romaji: Isshūkan buri ni harete, sentakumono o hoshita.
examples.tr: The sun came out for the first time in a week, so I hung out the laundry.

pitfalls: It needs a period (十年ぶり), not a point in time (十年前ぶり).
Not for the very first time in your life; it only fits something that has happened before.
